#1096 [Audit] IPC-4: Prototype can open unlimited URLs without a click (Low)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Triage note: Labelled critical but the audit rates it Low (a prototype can open unlimited URLs without a click). Suggest High.

Severity: Low
Category: Abuse of OS handlers
Location:

  • crates/ui-egui/src/present.rs:867-872 (OpenUrl), :1838-1841 (finish), :2690-2697 (AfterDelay), :725-735
  • crates/engine/src/doc_urls.rs:18,40-43 (mailto)
  • apps/figcraft/src/services.rs:304-306 (webbrowser::open)
    Summary: Prototype can open unlimited URLs (incl. mailto:?attach=) without a click.
    Status: Plausible

Verified (from code):

// present.rs:867-872
Action::OpenUrl { url } => {
    if figcraft_engine::doc_urls::openable(url) { self.urls.push(url.clone()); }
    true
}
// present.rs:1838-1841
fn finish(app: &mut FigApp, p: &mut Presenter) {
    for u in p.urls.drain(..) { app.services.open_url(&u); }
}
// doc_urls.rs:18,40-43
const WEB_SCHEMES: [&str; 3] = ["http", "https", "mailto"];
if scheme.eq_ignore_ascii_case("mailto") { return !rest.is_empty(); }
  • perform_at queues OpenUrl regardless of trigger; AfterDelay and waiting mouse triggers fire without any click, and finish opens them all with no confirmation, throttle, or per-URL prompt. mailto: passes with any non-empty remainder (including a pure query).

Impact: Opening/presenting an untrusted document can silently spawn N system/browser/mail opens — spam/phishing bait and unsolicited network egress.

Suggested fix: Require an explicit user gesture for OpenUrl, show a confirmation prompt before invoking the system opener, and drop mailto from WEB_SCHEMES (or treat it as click-only, confirmed).

#1088 [Audit] SRV-4: A correct join code resets the wrong-code streak (Low)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Triage note: Labelled critical but the audit rates it Low (a correct join code resets the wrong-code streak). Suggest Medium.

Severity: Low
Category: Brute-force limit bypass / DoS
Location:

  • apps/figcraft-server/src/abuse.rs:131-133
    Summary: A correct join code resets the wrong-code streak.
    Status: Confirmed

Verified (from code):

if ok || now.saturating_duration_since(a.wrong_at) > CODE_LOCKOUT {
    a.wrong = 0;
}
  • A correct code clears a.wrong for every block containing the ip. The global WRONG_CODES_PER_HOUR bucket is still charged on every wrong guess (line 127), and lockout triggers on 10 wrong in a row.

Impact: Mostly matters for an attacker sharing a /64-/56-/48 with a legitimate user whose successful joins clear the attacker's streak. The audit's two-IPv4 drain scenario is limited by the global bucket.

Suggested fix: To be strict, don't reset on ok (only decay by time) and track the streak per address regardless of peer successes; keep the global hourly bucket as the hard ceiling.

#1086 [Audit] COL-9: Image entries accepted under any hash; width/height unchecked (Low-Medium)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Triage note: Labelled critical but the audit rates it Low-Medium (image entries accepted under any hash). Suggest High.

Severity: Low-Medium
Category: Integrity
Location:

  • crates/collab/src/docprops.rs:287-290 (apply), :174-178 (image_of)
  • crates/collab/src/change.rs:240,307-316 (Entry::Image, id_space=None)
    Summary: Image entries are accepted under any hash; width and height are unchecked and there is no byte cap.
    Status: Confirmed

Verified (from code):

// docprops.rs:287-290
Entry::Image(k) => {
    let img = image_of(value)?;
    doc.images.insert(k.clone(), img);
}
// docprops.rs:174-178
fn image_of(value: &Json) -> Result<ImageData, Error> {
    let v: ImageValue = value.read("image")?;
    let bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.decode(v.bytes.as_bytes()).map_err(...)?;
    Ok(ImageData { bytes: Arc::new(bytes), width: v.width, height: v.height })
}
  • Nothing verifies k is a hash of bytes; width/height are taken from JSON with no bounds/cross-check; no size cap on bytes. Because Entry::Image's id_space() is None (change.rs:314), image Puts skip check_entries ownership validation too.

Impact: A participant can store arbitrary blobs keyed by arbitrary "hash" strings with arbitrary dimensions — memory amplification, forged cache keys, and oversized width/height metadata that renderers may trust for allocation.

Suggested fix: Validate decoded bytes (parse PNG/JPEG header for real dimensions), cap byte length and width/height, require k == computed hash of bytes (or hash server-side), and route image entries through the same ownership check.

#1071 [Audit] PLG-2: Plugins can read files and reach UNC paths via text.loadFont (Medium)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Medium
Category: Sandbox escape (file read, NTLM)
Location:

  • crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs:506-507 (text.loadFont path)
  • crates/engine/src/plugins.rs:124-153 (refusal())
  • crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:461-463 / file_access.rs:241-249 (read_capped)
    Summary: Plugins can text.loadFont {path} to read files and reach UNC paths (SMB/NTLM) — refusal() doesn't cover this command.
    Status: Confirmed (file read); NTLM Plausible

Verified (from code):

// cmd/text.rs:506-507
} else if let Some(path) = string(p, "path") {
    super::file::read_capped(&path, figcraft_text::fontdb::MAX_FONT_FILE)?
  • read_capped reads any file path from disk (bounded only by size).
  • refusal() covers image.place, variable.export/codeConnect.export/component.playground, codeConnect.import, variable.import — but not text.loadFont. The command is registered history = true (text.rs:499), so a Write-access plugin can read arbitrary files.

Impact: Sandbox escape: a Write plugin gets a file-read primitive (probe existence/content of any readable file via error text, timing, and the families output); on Windows a UNC path triggers an SMB connection.

Suggested fix: Extend refusal with a text.loadFont + path case (require data), mirroring the image.place rule.

#1064 [Audit] ENG-3: Stale next_id makes paste_nodes overwrite existing nodes (High)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: High
Category: Integrity / DoS
Location:

  • crates/doc/src/lib.rs:136-145 (alloc), :166 (next_id), :846-848 (paste_nodes)
    Summary: Stale next_id from a file makes paste_nodes silently overwrite existing nodes; a file with next_id=1 makes Ctrl+D collide with existing nodes, potentially creating a self-parent cycle.
    Status: Confirmed missing check; cycle Plausible

Verified (from code):

// lib.rs:136-145
fn alloc(&mut self) -> NodeId {
    let id = NodeId(self.next);
    let next = self.next.saturating_add(1);
    if self.owns(NodeId(next)) { self.next = next; }
    id
}
// lib.rs:166
next_id: IdAlloc,        // deserialized as-is (transparent serde), no validation
// lib.rs:846-848 (paste_nodes)
self.reserve_ids(*new_id);
self.nodes.insert(*new_id, Arc::new(c));
self.dirty.touch(*new_id);
  • paste_nodes inserts with no contains_key check (unlike insert() at lib.rs:425-428 which errors on duplicate). A remap collision silently overwrites an existing node.

Impact: Crafted/corrupt files can set next_id arbitrarily; id collisions make later inserts fail, huge values freeze allocation at the last id, and colliding pastes silently destroy nodes (a self-parent cycle if the colliding id is the copy's own parent).

Suggested fix: Validate next_id on load (advance past the max node id); make paste_nodes detect/return collisions; make alloc error or move to a fresh space instead of returning the last id.

#1056 [Audit] ENG-1: Document-named library paths reach UNC shares (NTLM leak) (High (Windows))

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: High (Windows) / Low elsewhere
Category: SSRF / credential leak
Location:

  • crates/ui-egui/src/assets_panel.rs:277-284 (load path)
  • crates/engine/src/library.rs:481-508 (load_limited -> stat/read_file)
  • crates/engine/src/library_server.rs:130-139 (the only is_local check)
    Summary: Library paths stored in a document are opened by the Assets panel with no craft_docpath::is_local check; a \\attacker\share\lib.figcraft link opens an SMB session and leaks the user's NTLM hash on open.
    Status: Confirmed (re-checked)

Verified (from code):

// assets_panel.rs:277-284
let paths: Vec<String> = doc.libraries.enabled.iter().map(|l| l.path.clone()).collect();
for p in &paths { let _ = app.session.libraries.load(p); }
// library.rs:481-508
pub fn load_limited(&mut self, path: &str, max_bytes: u64) -> Result<Arc<PublishedLibrary>> {
    if crate::library_server::is_server_link(path) { ... }
    let stamp = stat(path); ... read_file(path) ...
  • stat/read_file go through file_access::metadata/open (library.rs:543-564), with no is_local check.
  • The only is_local check is in fetch_library (library_server.rs:130-139) — bypassed by the Assets panel's direct Cache::load.

Impact: A path stored in a document is read from any local path, including UNC/network shares; on Windows this sends credentials to a remote share / contacts a network host.

Suggested fix: Add the craft_docpath::is_local check at the top of Cache::load_limited (or route the Assets refresh through Session::load_library).

#1055 [Audit] PLG-1: Read-only plugin can upload the document over the network (High)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: High
Category: Sandbox escape / exfiltration
Location:

  • crates/engine/src/plugins.rs:98-119 (DENIED list), :124-153 (refusal())
  • crates/plugin/src/manifest.rs:78-79 (allows())
  • crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs:44-47 (history=false), :363-364 (net upload)
  • crates/engine/src/background.rs:129-146 (Session::net)
    Summary: The plugin deny list does not include library.publishToServer; with an empty commands list permissions.allows() returns true, so a default read-only plugin can upload the entire open document to an attacker's server.
    Status: Confirmed in the engine (re-checked); network upload not run

Verified (from code):

  • DENIED (plugins.rs:98-119) has library.add, libraries., collab., file. etc. — but not library.publishToServer.
  • allows() (manifest.rs:78-79): self.commands.is_empty() || ... — empty allowlist permits everything.
  • library.publishToServer is registered with history = false (cmd/library.rs:44-47), so refusal()'s read-access guard (plugins.rs:149-151) never triggers.
  • publish_to_server (cmd/library.rs:363-364) calls s.net(NetRequest::Upload(opts)); Session::net hands it to the live link (background.rs:129-146).

Impact: A plugin with the default manifest (Read, empty commands) can upload the full open document to a server — data exfiltration bypassing the network/file sandbox.

Suggested fix: Add "library.publishToServer" to DENIED (or gate NetRequest::Upload for plugin-originated calls at the Host::call boundary).

#1054 [Audit] COL-1: Client-id takeover through Hello.resume (High)

maintainer labelregression · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: High
Category: Authn/authz
Location:

  • crates/collab/src/server.rs:269 (filter), :270 (session-full skip)
  • crates/collab-net/src/hub.rs:1389,1399-1401 (takeover)
    Summary: Resume is authorised by public (session, client_id): any participant, including a view-only one, can take over another participant's id, including the host's.
    Status: Confirmed (re-checked)

Verified (from code):

// server.rs:269
let resume = hello.resume.filter(|r| r.session == self.session && self.issued.contains_key(&r.client_id));
// server.rs:270
if self.peers.len() >= self.limits.max_peers && resume.is_none_or(|r| !self.peers.contains_key(&r.client_id)) {
// hub.rs:1389, 1399-1401
let old = room.ids.insert(id, conn).filter(|old| *old != conn);
...
if let Some(c) = old.and_then(|old| self.conns.remove(&old)) { shutdown(&c.sock); }
  • Resume carries only {session, client_id, seq} (message.rs:90-97); the session id and all peer ids are broadcast to everyone (Welcome/PeerJoined).
  • The hub maps id -> conn, hands the id to the new connection, and shuts down the old socket.
  • The is_none_or at :270 means a resumed id that is already a peer skips the "session full" refusal.

Impact: Any participant (anyone holding the shared invite token) can hijack any live client id — including the host's — by sending Hello{resume: Some(Resume{session, client_id, seq})}. The victim's connection is force-closed and the attacker inherits the victim's identity and control privileges.

Suggested fix: Issue a random per-client secret when an id is first granted, store it in issued, require it in Resume, and check it in the filter at :269; also refuse resuming the host's local id.

#965 [Bug] FigCraft 0.8.0 fails to open on Windows 11: WGPU Parent device is lost

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-21 by nanopink · updated 2026-10-21

Description

Opening the installed FigCraft desktop app fails before the main window appears. A native FigCraft error dialog reports a WGPU device loss.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Launch the installed FigCraft 0.8.0 desktop app on the Windows system described below.
  2. Observe the startup error dialog instead of the main window.

The failure was reported with a screenshot. Repeatability and the triggering graphics adapter/backend have not been established.

Expected behavior

FigCraft opens its main window normally.

Actual behavior

The screenshot's error message reads:

FigCraft couldn't open its window: WGPU error: Parent device is lost

The dialog also suggests updating the graphics driver or starting from Command Prompt with:

set WGPU_BACKEND=gl
figcraft.exe

That suggested workaround has not been tested as part of this report.

Environment

  • Installed FigCraft version: 0.8.0, as reported by the Windows installed-app registration.
  • OS: Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit, version 10.0.26200 (build 26200).
  • Installed graphics adapters and driver versions:
    • NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti — 32.0.16.1088.
    • AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics — 32.0.21030.2001.
  • Both adapters are listed by Windows; which one FigCraft selected is unknown.

Related reports checked

  • #261 reports failure to launch on Windows 10 with FigCraft 0.5.1 and is closed. It does not include this error message, so it is unclear whether it had the same cause.
  • Searches across open and closed issues for the exact device-loss message and related WGPU/startup terms did not find a matching report.

The error above was transcribed from the reporter's error.png screenshot. No root cause is asserted.

2 comments
ticket-craft[bot] · 2026-10-21

Possibly related: #261, storytold/soundcraft#185 and storytold/cadcraft#608.

nanopink · 2026-10-21

Follow-up: tested fresh launches of the installed FigCraft 0.8.0 executable directly from PowerShell on the same system.

Launch configuration Result
WGPU_BACKEND unset Reproduces WGPU error: Parent device is lost; the main window does not open.
WGPU_BACKEND=gl Opens the home screen successfully and responds.
WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan Opens the app/editor successfully and responds.

For the default launch, WGPU_BACKEND was confirmed absent from the process, user, and machine environment. It was also explicitly removed from the child process's inherited environment before launch. Each configuration was tested in a separate FigCraft process.

The default-launch stderr enumerates DX12 and GL adapters, then reports the following before the device-loss error (excerpt; embedded line breaks simplified):

ERROR wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("DXC compile error: warning: DXIL signing library (dxil.dll,libdxil.so) not found. Resulting DXIL will not be signed for use in release environments."))
ERROR eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
ERROR figcraft::startup: FigCraft couldn't open its window: WGPU error: Parent device is lost

This narrows the failure to the default graphics initialization path on this system and establishes two working startup workarounds. The missing DXIL signing library is a diagnostic clue; it has not been established as the root cause. These checks verify startup and a responsive window, rather than a full editing/rendering test.

Summary

FigCraft 0.6.0 crashes on the main thread about 17 seconds after launch with an
uncaught Objective-C exception thrown from AppKit's Touch Bar finder code.

Environment

  • FigCraft: 0.6.0 (ai.storyteller.figcraft)
  • macOS: 27.0.1 (26A434)
  • Hardware: MacBookPro17,1 (Apple M1, 8 GB), ARM-64 native (not Rosetta)
  • Display: built-in 2560x1600 Retina
  • Low Power Mode: on
  • Time since wake: ~837 s (crash happened ~14 min after wake from sleep)

Expected behavior

App keeps running.

Actual behavior

App terminates with EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP) on the main thread.

Steps to reproduce

on app launch
Reproducible? Yes

Key crash details

Exception: EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP), triggered by thread 0 (main)

Application Specific Backtrace (top frames):
__exceptionPreprocess
objc_exception_throw
-[NSObject(NSKeyValueObserverRegistration) _removeObserver:forProperty:]
-[NSObject(NSKeyValueObserverRegistration) removeObserver:forKeyPath:]
-[_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate]
___NSTouchBarFinderSetNeedsUpdateOnMain_block_invoke_2
NSDisplayCycleObserverInvoke

...

winit ... EventLoop::run_on_demand

Analysis

The throw originates entirely inside AppKit (KVO observer removal in the

bflatastic · 2026-10-18

Thanks for the report and the crash log, @oshanz! This is a known AppKit crash that affects all the Crafting Apps on Touch Bar Macs (tracked in craft-libs#3). The Touch Bar's observer follows the window's view, which the accessibility layer swaps out, so tearing the window down throws on the next display update. Your MacBook Pro has a Touch Bar, which is why you see it. A fix for the quit path is in progress: after everything is saved, FigCraft will end the process on macOS instead of tearing the window down.

Could you tell us whether it happens only when quitting (or closing a window), or also with the app just open, and whether it still happens on 0.7.0?

If you haven't already, come say hi on our Discord: https://discord.gg/artcraft

bflatastic · 2026-10-18

An update: #791 (merged) makes FigCraft end its process on macOS after it has saved everything on quit (preferences, recovery copies, live-session goodbyes), so the window teardown that throws the Touch Bar exception never runs. It also fixes a data-loss case we found on the way: Cmd+Q from the menu bar skipped the unsaved-changes question and then removed the recovery copies; they're now kept and reopen at the next start.

We couldn't try it on a Mac. Please let us know if it still crashes on the next release, and especially whether it ever happens with the app just open (not quitting or closing a window). That case would need a separate fix, so I'm keeping this issue open until we hear back.

oshanz · 2026-10-18

Hi @bflatastic

Thanks for the quick fix! To answer your questions:

  • My MacBook Pro does have a Touch Bar.
  • I’ve updated to 0.7.0. There is no crash on launch, and it doesn’t happen when the app is just open. My original report may have been wrong. I was testing multiple Craft apps at the time, so I might have misattributed the event. I also noticed the same exception in all the apps, including the launcher.
  • Quitting with Cmd+Q doesn’t throw an exception either.
  • It still crashes when I close the window with the red close button.

#480 Control channel (--control) accepts commands without authentication

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-15 by Losminek · updated 2026-10-15

Triage note: Same problem as audit #1072 (in progress): fix once, close both.

Split out of #468. Checked against main (8482c3e).

apps/figcraft/src/control_server.rs (around 65–118) listens on loopback and executes any newline-delimited JSON it receives. A line that isn't valid JSON gets an error response, but the connection stays open. Any local process can drive the app while --control is on, and a web page sending a request to the loopback port may be able to as well. It's opt-in, so the impact is limited, but there's no key at all.

Same class elsewhere: storytold/gridcraft#777, storytold/deckcraft#263, storytold/vectorcraft#2100. WordCraft fixed it with a per-session key file and by closing the connection on a non-JSON first line (storytold/wordcraft#124, storytold/wordcraft#72; LightCraft did the latter in storytold/lightcraft#94). PhotoCraft's control server requires a bearer token.

I use FigCraft through figcraft-cli mcp --attach with Claude Code and Codex, so I'd like to add
what I saw on the release build and a suggestion that might unblock #500.

What I saw on v0.6.0 (macOS release build, 2026-10-15)

  • The listener accepts any newline-delimited {"id","method","params"} line from any client that
    can reach 127.0.0.1:<port>. There's no key and no file confinement, so that includes
    ui.screenshot {path} / ui.render {path} writing to any path the user can write, and
    app.quit closing every window without asking about unsaved changes.
  • The browser path described in #589 is reachable on v0.6.0: a request a web page makes the browser
    send to the control port gets "bad JSON" replies for its request/header lines, and a valid JSON
    line in the body is then dispatched. I'm not attaching a page; the test in #589 covers it.

#589 fixes the second point on main, thanks! Since it landed after v0.6.0, could it go into a
patch release? Until then, anyone running v0.6.0 with --control on is exposed to any page open
in their browser. The workaround is to turn --control on only for an agent session and quit
FigCraft afterwards.

A token design that doesn't change how people connect

I understand #500 is on hold because --control exits without FIGCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN and every
client has to be given the secret. PhotoCraft solves the same problem in a way that avoids both,
and it would keep the Crafting Apps consistent:

  1. figcraft --control <port> --control-token-file <path> (env: FIGCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN_FILE).
    If the file doesn't exist, the app creates it with a fresh 256-bit token (mode 0600 on Unix,
    user-only ACL on Windows); an existing file is reused. With no token or file configured, the
    app generates a per-launch token and prints it to stderr, or, nicer for #571, writes it to a
    default 0600 file in the app's config/runtime dir. It never refuses to start.

  2. First-frame auth, once per connection:
    {"id":"auth","method":"auth","params":{"token":"<64 hex>"}}. Nothing else is dispatched
    before it succeeds; a failed or missing auth gets a generic error and the connection closes.
    This also covers the "parse before auth" point from the #500 review: the first frame can be
    capped at a few KiB and given a short absolute deadline, and full 32 MiB lines are only read
    after authentication. Unlike a per-request token field, every later line stays as it is today.

  3. Keep #589's rule (first non-JSON line closes the connection). With first-frame auth it's
    defence in depth: an HTTP request line can never be a valid auth frame.

  4. figcraft-cli mcp --attach <port> --control-token-file <path> (env:
    FIGCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN_FILE; --control-token / FIGCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN as a fallback). The
    CLI reads the file and sends the auth frame on every (re)connect. This matters for MCP
    clients: their config (.mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json, claude mcp add) then holds
    a path, not the secret, e.g.

    "figcraft-app": {
  "command": "/path/to/figcraft-cli",
  "args": ["mcp", "--attach", "7979", "--control-token-file", "/path/to/figcraft-control.token"]
}

    With an env-var-only token, the secret has to sit in plain text in that config's env block,
    and an app opened from the Dock or Start menu doesn't inherit a shell's environment anyway.
    A file also stays out of the environment that child processes inherit (point 4 in the #500
    review).

This fits #571 well: the "Connect an AI agent" window could create the default token file and put
--control-token-file <path> in the snippet it copies, so turning the channel on from the app
stays one click and the copied config contains no secret.

For reference, PhotoCraft documents this in docs/control-protocol.md and docs/mcp.md (the
--control-token-file and --bridge sections). PR #500's loopback-only resolution check and
no-replay behaviour would carry over unchanged.

Separately: turning on GitHub private vulnerability reporting, or adding a SECURITY.md like
PhotoCraft's, would give the next report like this a private route.

#1219 Thai, Lao, Khmer and Burmese text has no line-break opportunities: lines break mid-word

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-23 by Salah1St · updated 2026-10-23

Text written without spaces between words (Thai, Lao, Khmer, Burmese) only breaks where it overflows the box: mid-word (พัฒนาซอ|ฟต์แวร์, inside ซอฟต์แวร์ "software"), and even between a leading vowel and the consonant it is written before (จัดทำเ|อกสาร, ที่มีโ|ครงสร้าง), which no Thai reader accepts.

crates/text/src/breaks.rs implements a subset of UAX #14 with a pairwise break_between(a, b). Thai letters fall into Class::Other, which never breaks inside a run, so a Thai paragraph is one unbreakable word until the emergency break splits it anywhere. UAX 14 puts these scripts in class SA (complex context): finding their break opportunities needs a dictionary or a model.

Repro (0.10.0)

  1. Text tool, a fixed-width box 160 px wide, Noto Sans Thai at 16 px.
  2. Type or paste ระบบช่วยให้ทีมพัฒนาซอฟต์แวร์จัดทำเอกสารที่มีโครงสร้างได้ในที่เดียว (a synthetic sentence: "the system helps software teams produce structured documents in one place").
  3. The lines are ระบบช่วยให้ทีมพัฒนาซอ / ฟต์แวร์จัดทำเอกสารที่มีโ / ครงสร้างได้ในที่เดียว: ซอฟต์แวร์ ("software") and โครงสร้าง ("structure") are split, the second right after its leading vowel. At 120 px, จัดทำเอกสาร breaks as จัดทำเ|อกสาร.

Proposal

  • Full: compute the break opportunities of a paragraph with icu_segmenter::LineSegmenter (pure Rust, from the Unicode ICU4X project, with dictionary or LSTM models for Thai, Lao, Khmer and Burmese) instead of the pairwise break_between, at least for SA runs. Cost: the Thai data adds roughly 0.3–1 MB to the wasm; with tests, about 3–5 days.
  • Minimal, meanwhile: in the emergency break, never break before a combining mark (U+0E31, U+0E34–U+0E3A, U+0E47–U+0E4E) or after a leading vowel (U+0E40–U+0E44). About half a day to a day.

Workaround for text that tools generate: insert U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE between words (a Thai word segmenter such as PyThaiNLP's newmm can do this) before the text goes into the file. FigCraft already breaks there, since breaks.rs classes U+200B as a space, and lines then break only between words (#1218 keeps justified text from widening U+200B). Text typed by hand in the editor still breaks anywhere.

#1157 Ctrl+S does nothing while a panel field has the keyboard

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by switch87 · updated 2026-10-22

Ctrl+S does nothing while a field in a panel has the keyboard (X, Y, W, H, a colour, a name). There is no message, the tab keeps its unsaved dot, and the file on disk doesn't change. Click on the canvas or press Escape first, and Ctrl+S saves. If you don't know that, it looks like the file can't be saved.

I ran into this with a file made by figcraft-cli mcp: Ctrl+S did nothing, and closing the window only offered "Close without saving" and "Cancel".

Reproduced on main at 9ec80bf (Linux, X11), on a copy of that file on an exFAT drive and in /tmp, so it doesn't depend on the file or the file system:

  1. Open a .figcraft file and select a layer.
  2. Nudge it with an arrow key (the tab shows the unsaved dot).
  3. Click in the Y field of the Design panel.
  4. Press Ctrl+S: nothing happens, the file's modification time stays the same.
  5. Press Escape, then Ctrl+S: the file is saved.

The cause is in shortcuts::handle: while a field has the keyboard, it returns before it looks at any key, so the save shortcut never runs.

Expected: Ctrl+S (and Shift+Ctrl+S) save from a field too, with what was typed in the field committed first, as most desktop apps do.

I'm working on this.

#1131 [Audit] Minor 22: Plain ws:// on the LAN

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Low
Category: Minor (network / credential exposure on LAN)
Location:

  • crates/collab-net/src/host.rs:72 — TcpListener::bind(cfg.addr): the desktop host listens on plain TCP, no TLS
  • crates/collab-net/src/invite.rs:44-48 — Endpoint::plain(host) sets secure: false → URL is ws://host:port/
  • crates/collab-net/src/invite.rs:9-12 — the token is not in the WebSocket URL; the client sends it in its Hello frame after connecting
  • crates/collab-net/src/host.rs:50-58 — OneFile::admit authenticates with the token

Summary: The desktop app hosts collaboration sessions on a plain ws:// WebSocket listener with no encryption. The secret session token is sent over that unencrypted connection in the Hello message.

Detail (from code):

  • Host::start binds a bare TcpListener (host.rs:72) and the hub serves the WebSocket directly — there is no TLS layer in the embedded host.
  • Invites for a hosted session are built with Endpoint::plain (invite.rs:44-48, invite.rs:111-113), which gives secure = false, so the connection URL is ws://host:port/ and wss:// is never used here.
  • The token is deliberately kept out of the URL (invite.rs:9-12; also asserted in driver_tests.rs:103), but it is then transmitted in the client's Hello frame — still over the unencrypted ws:// channel.
  • Admission is token-only (host.rs:50-58): whoever holds the token edits the session.

Impact: On a shared LAN, anyone who can observe traffic (or ARP-spoof) can capture the session token and join or edit the hosted session. Because the host binds the configured address (any local interface, not just loopback), this is reachable from other machines on the network. Severity is capped at Low because the shared-document threat model treats LAN peers as semi-trusted and sniffing is passive.

Suggested fix (options):

  • Serve the hosted session over TLS (e.g. generate a self-signed certificate for the LAN host, or instruct users to host through figcraft-server behind a TLS reverse proxy).
  • Shorten token lifetime / rotate the token per session, and bound it to the invite link.
  • At minimum, document the LAN exposure and offer a setting that restricts hosting to loopback.

Source: FigCraft security & robustness audit (rev 9ec80bf2, 2026-10-22) — AUDIT.md (Minor section), verified against the workspace code.

#1090 [Audit] SRV-6: Any log read error discards confirmed edits (Low)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Low
Category: Data loss
Location:

  • apps/figcraft-server/src/store.rs:1113,1155,1170
  • apps/figcraft-server/src/disk.rs (read_capped/read_log)
    Summary: Any log read error (or a lowered cap) discards confirmed edits by starting a new log.
    Status: Confirmed (path)

Verified (from code):

// store.rs:1113
match disk::read_capped(&dir.join(LOG), self.cfg.max_file_bytes).and_then(|b| disk::read_log(&b)) {
// store.rs:1155
Err(why) => issues.push(format!("file {file}: {why}; starting a new log")),
// store.rs:1170
_ => self.rewrite(file, generation + 1, &server).map_err(|e| e.why)?,
  • Any Err from read_capped (IO error or log over the cap) or read_log leaves fresh_log = true, so line 1170 rewrites a new snapshot and empty log — discarding previously flushed and acknowledged log entries (only the "damaged end" path drops the tail).

Impact: A transient/temporary log-read failure silently loses confirmed edits — a durability violation (clients were told the edits were saved).

Suggested fix: On log read failure never overwrite — quarantine the old log (rename aside), refuse to open or surface recovery, and only start fresh after the old log was successfully read/replayed.

#1084 [Audit] ENG-4: Mutually containing components aren't refused (Medium)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Medium
Category: DoS (memory, CPU)
Location:

  • crates/engine/src/components.rs:263-270 (create_instance_at), :516-526,574-585,615 (sync_instance)
  • crates/engine/src/cmd/component.rs:279-285 (place), :880-883 (swap_instance)
  • crates/engine/src/components.rs:1597-1598 (rebuild_instances 64 rounds), :40 (MAX_DEPTH=16)
    Summary: Mutually containing component instances aren't refused; sync can grow without bound (or silently truncate at 16/64).
    Status: Plausible

Verified (from code):

// components.rs:263-270
if doc.is_ancestor(component, parent) {
    return Err(DocError::Invalid("an instance can't be placed inside its own main component".into()));
}
// cmd/component.rs:279-285
if doc.is_ancestor(c, slot.parent) || slot.parent == c {
    slot = crate::drop::DropSlot { parent: page, index: None, line: None };
}
// cmd/component.rs:880-883
if doc.is_ancestor(c, i) { return Err("an instance can't show the component it is inside".into()); }
  • Containment is refused only at these three entry points via ancestry (plus direct equality). sync_instance rebuilds the full subtree of the component; nested instances recurse via sync_instance_depth guarded only by MAX_DEPTH = 16; rebuild_instances runs at most 64 rounds.

Impact: Mutually containing structures via sets/indirect references aren't blocked; deep nested-instance chains are silently truncated (16 levels / 64 rounds) instead of rejected, leaving possibly stale/mismatched instances.

Suggested fix: Also guard on owning set/variant containment, and convert truncation into an error rather than a silent stop.

// paint.rs:140
let (hash, iw, ih, content) = match lone {
    Some(l) => l,

// import/mod.rs:103

  • No authentication/authorization anywhere on the socket. It binds loopback, accepts up to 8 plain-TCP connections, and every JSON line is dispatched straight to handle — engine.execute runs any engine command, ui.screenshot/ui.render write to any named path (unconfined by default).

Impact: Any local process (or a browser via DNS rebinding) can read the open document, mutate it, trigger app.quit, open system URLs, and overwrite any file the user can write.

Suggested fix: Require a per-connection secret token (generated at launch, verified as the first line); restrict to loopback; add a method allow-list; gate write paths behind configured automation roots.

#1068 [Audit] COL-6: Pre-authentication slowloris (Medium)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Medium
Category: DoS (pre-auth)
Location:

  • crates/collab-net/src/hub.rs:824-841 (pre-hello loop), :854 (per-read timeout), :857 (health_check)
  • crates/collab-net/src/limits.rs:63-74 (max_connections, max_per_address=0)
    Summary: No overall handshake deadline; pings keep unauthenticated slots alive (slowloris). 64 sockets pinged every 9s fill all slots; the desktop host has no per-address limit.
    Status: Confirmed

Verified (from code):

// hub.rs:824-841
fn next_message(...) -> Result<Option<(ClientMsg, usize)>, String> {
    loop {
        return match ws.read() {
            ...
            Ok(Message::Ping(_) | Message::Pong(_) | Message::Frame(_)) => continue,   // :833
// hub.rs:854
if stream.set_read_timeout(Some(limits.hello_timeout)).is_err() || ... { return; }
  • hello_timeout (10s default) is a per-read timeout; each read() that returns a ping re-arms it, and tungstenite auto-answers pings. health_check's deadline only bounds the pre-handshake /healthz peek, not the WebSocket hello.
  • NetLimits::default() sets max_per_address: 0 — no per-address cap; only the 64 max_connections slots limit.

Impact: An unauthenticated client can hold one of the 64 connection slots forever by pinging every <10s — a slowloris DoS on a default desktop host.

Suggested fix: Record an absolute deadline at serve entry and enforce it in the pre-hello loop regardless of ping traffic; optionally cap pre-hello connections per address.

#1065 [Audit] COL-3: O(n^2) sibling placement on the single hub thread (Medium-High)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Medium-High
Category: DoS (CPU, server-wide)

    Summary: Placement counts preceding siblings linearly per Create/Set; one batch of 500k creates under one parent is ~1.25e11 comparisons on the live-hub thread.
    Status: Confirmed (running time estimated)

Verified (from code):

fn slot(&self, siblings: &[NodeId], id: NodeId, key: &str) -> usize {
    siblings.iter().filter(|c| **c != id && (self.key(**c), **c) < (key, id)).count()
}
  • apply_one calls slot once per Create (:197), per parent Set (:211), per position Set (:227). Creating/inserting n siblings under one parent in a batch is O(n²).

Impact: Large single-batch sibling inserts/orders degrade quadratically — a CPU DoS within the (capped) batch size, and slow large pastes/reorders.

Suggested fix: Binary-search the rank over the sorted (key, id) order (partition_point), making each placement O(log n).

#1063 [Audit] COL-2: Quadratic fixes() for a refused batch (High)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Category: DoS (out-of-memory abort, server)

  • crates/collab/src/server.rs:508 (fn fixes), :544-555
    Summary: A refused batch that deletes a ~20,000-deep chain re-emits the whole subtree of every deleted id (~N^2/2 Create changes, tens of GB) on the hub thread.

for id in gone {
    match doc.node(id) {
        Some(_) => { for d in doc.subtree(id) {
            if let Some(n) = doc.node(d) { nodes.push(create_change(n, self.state.key(d))?); }
        } }
        None => nodes.push(Change::Delete { id }),
    }
}
  • For every deleted id that still exists, doc.subtree(id) enumerates the whole subtree and create_change rebuilds a full Create for every node — no dedup, O(N²) worst case.

Impact: A refused (attacker-authored) batch forces the server to generate/send a quadratically large fixes payload — CPU and network amplification / DoS, and duplicate nodes in the rollback.

Suggested fix: Deduplicate before emitting (union of affected ids via a BTreeSet), emit one create_change per unique surviving node, and cap total fix size to limits.

    Summary: Each nested isolated layer or mask allocates a full-view pixmap; the total is unbounded (64 nested groups with drop shadows -> tens of GB).
    Status: Confirmed

Verified (from code):

// draw.rs:507-519 (draw_layer)
let vis = dev.intersect(view);
let (w, h) = (vis.x1.ceil() - x0, vis.y1.ceil() - y0);
...

// draw.rs:786-815 (draw_masked)

let Some(mut mask_px) = Pixmap::new(w, h) else { return };
...
let mut tmp = Pixmap::new(w, h);
...
let Some(mut layer) = Pixmap::new(w, h) else { return };
  • draw_layer clips to vis = dev ∩ view (+ <=2048px effect margin) — bounded.
  • draw_masked allocates mask_px, tmp and layer — all full-canvas, with no culling, regardless of how small mask/content is.

Impact: Any masked group allocates 2-3 full-canvas RGBA buffers (e.g. 4K ≈ 3×33MB), and nested masked groups stack them — predictable memory pressure; small masks far from content still cost full-canvas memory.

Suggested fix: Compute the union rect of mask and content, intersect with the view, and allocate/clip only that region.

#912 MCP: inspect_document with allPages exceeds the 10 MiB client read buffer and kills the server

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-20 by IbrahimElmourchidi · updated 2026-10-20

Summary

The headless MCP server (figcraft-cli mcp) can emit a single JSON-RPC response larger than the 10 MiB default read buffer of the MCP TypeScript SDK's StdioClientTransport. When it does, the client aborts the read and closes the pipe, the server dies with stdio: Broken pipe (os error 32), and the client marks the server permanently failed — every later call returns Connection closed until the client is restarted.

On a 1 MB design file this is reachable with an ordinary inspect_document call.

Environment

  • figcraft-cli 0.7.0 (FigCraft 0.7.0, 47438dd4a2e8b49a7e6bb3dfd480262dadc37f12)
  • Linux 6.18.4-1-liquorix-amd64
  • Client: OpenCode 2.0.32, MCP stdio transport (SDK maxBufferSize default = 10,485,760 bytes)
  • Document: 1.0 MB .figcraft, 4 pages, 13,818 shapes

Steps to reproduce

  1. Start the server on stdio:
    figcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root <dir> --automation-write-root <dir>
  2. open_file the document.
  3. Call inspect_document with { "allPages": true, "depth": 5 }.

Expected

The document, or a bounded/paginated response with an explicit truncation marker.

Actual

Client log:

mcp transport error error="ReadBuffer exceeded maximum size of 10485760 bytes"
mcp transport error error="MCP server process exited with code 1: figcraft MCP server (headless ...) on stdio
error: stdio: Broken pipe (os error 32)"
failed to call MCP tool error="Connection closed: ..."

The server is then dead for the rest of the session. Reading exactly 10,485,760 bytes from its stdout and closing the pipe reproduces the exit deterministically (exit code 1, same stderr line), so the crash is entirely a payload-size problem, not a timeout or a bad argument.

Measured payload growth (inspect_document, allPages: true)

depth response size vs 10 MiB cap
1 53,766 B 0.5%
2 593,174 B 5.7%
3 4,095,444 B 39%
4 (default) 8,896,314 B 85%
5 12,348,817 B 118% — crash
99 / full 20,718,923 B 198%

The default depth of 4 already produces 85% of the cap on this file, so the default call sits just under the cliff and any growth in the document pushes it over.

Unaffected paths, for contrast: screenshot of a 3840×5419 board = 254,395 B; resources/read figcraft://document = 23,496 B; initialize = 1,842 B.

Why this happens

  • MCP stdio is newline-delimited JSON: one tool result is one message, so the entire payload must fit the client's read buffer. There is no streaming of a partial message.
  • 10 MiB is the SDK default (STDIO_DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFER_SIZE in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk), not a FigCraft constant, and most clients do not raise it. The SDK exposes a maxBufferSize transport option, but hosts commonly leave it unset.
  • inspect_document returns every property for every node (absoluteBounds, fills, strokes, effects, component links, overrides, bound variables). On this design that is ≈1,500 bytes per shape, so a 13.8k-shape document is ~20 MB.

Suggested fixes

Any one of these removes the failure mode:

  1. Bound the response — add maxBytes (or maxShapes) to inspect_document; truncate with an explicit marker plus a cursor to continue.
  2. Paginate — offset/limit over page children or a page selector, so a large document is walked in slices.
  3. Cheaper default — set the default depth to 2 (593 KB here) and document that depth multiplies payload size; keep deep dumps opt-in.
  4. Prevent the single giant message — e.g. return a document id and let the caller request per-page/per-subtree slices, rather than one all-pages tree.
  5. Document the cost in the tool description so clients and agents can budget before calling.

A note in the tool description stating "depth > 4 with allPages can exceed common 10 MiB MCP client buffers" would already prevent the crash.

Additional notes

  • get_node({ id, depth }) is a good escape hatch today: scoping to a subtree keeps each message small while still allowing unlimited depth. Worth pointing agents at it in the failure message.
  • This is not specific to one client — any host using the SDK's stdio transport with default settings will kill the server the same way.

Hamza0101 · 2026-10-20

A second way to the same crash, found while testing the fix in #915: get_node has no size limit either, and it is the tool the shallower-tree marker tells callers to use for the rest.

Measured through figcraft-cli mcp on a document whose page holds one frame with 15,000 rectangles:

call message
inspect_document {depth: 64, allPages: true} 14.29 MiB (this issue)
get_node {id, depth: 64} 10.51 MiB

Both are over the 10 MiB STDIO_DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFER_SIZE, so either one ends the session the way you describe.

The width is what makes get_node hard: its 15,000 children are all at depth 1, so depth 1 is already 9.12 MiB of text and depth 0 has no children at all — reducing the depth cannot fix it. #915 now gives get_node the same maxBytes and, for that case, a window over the children with the offset to ask for next:

get_node depth 64    8.00 MiB, children 11427 of 15000 from 0, next 11427

Worth knowing if you are working around this today: get_node on a wide frame is not a safe substitute on a release build, and inspect_document with allPages is not the only call that can reach the limit.

This looks fixed since 0.6.0, though I cannot confirm it against your file.

The importer does read the per-instance swap: overriddenSymbolID is picked up in crates/format/src/fig/map.rs both when collecting override targets and when resolving an instance's main, so a nested instance whose icon was swapped should resolve to the swapped component rather than the default.

Five tests in crates/format/src/fig/source_identity_tests.rs cover that, including the shape your dump shows — a swap on an instance nested inside a frame:

  • visible_instance_override_retains_and_links_hidden_cached_main
  • visible_component_default_swap_retains_hidden_cached_main
  • selected_swapped_main_owns_alias_resolution_scope
  • swapped_children_use_current_main_through_frames_and_multiple_siblings
  • explicit_frame_to_instance_resets_children_to_the_resolved_main

All 22 of that file's tests pass on main @ 64423c5.

What I cannot do from here is reproduce your actual file: 11 buttons on one screen falling back to the default could still be a case these synthetic messages do not cover (an external main, a swap applied at a different level of nesting, or a variant set in between). If you still see it on a build newer than 0.6.0, attaching the .fig — or even just the inspect dump of one affected button and its main — would settle whether there is anything left here.

#387 fix(macos): shipped DMG app fails strict codesign verification with FinderInfo

classified in this triage · opened 2026-10-15 by coygeek · updated 2026-10-15

Triage note: Release packaging: the app inside the shipped universal DMG fails strict codesign verification because of com.apple.FinderInfo detritus. Strip extended attributes (xattr -cr) before signing in the release job and add a codesign --verify --strict --deep step to CI so it can't regress.

Summary

The app in the official universal macOS DMG fails strict signature verification with resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed. This occurs directly on the app inside the mounted read-only image, before copying it, and also on a ditto copy. Removing only com.apple.FinderInfo recursively from the disposable copy restores strict verification, and Gatekeeper accepts the resulting copy as notarized. This is a packaging validation failure; GUI launch was not tested and no launch failure is claimed.

Runtime or environment

  • Release: v0.6.0, currently the latest published release; asset figcraft-0.6.0-macos-universal.dmg.
  • Download SHA-256: 26385f23a95190458081c20efac0c1d86546b899ccbdabc7364f396dcacc7cc4, matching both the GitHub asset digest and the release's SHA256SUMS.txt.
  • Source: default main and the release tag both resolve to 833f0d2c27f0acbae5394848930ae531fc89c724. Their packaging/macos/package.sh files are identical.
  • Fresh reproduction: macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434, Apple silicon. lipo -archs reports x86_64 arm64 for the copied app executable.

Steps to reproduce

On macOS with GitHub CLI authenticated or otherwise able to download the public release, run the following in a disposable directory. These are the same download, mount, verification and copy operations used in the fresh reproduction. The attribute-removal operation modifies only the disposable copy.

work="$(mktemp -d /tmp/figcraft-check.XXXXXX)"
cd "$work"
gh release download v0.6.0 -R storytold/figcraft \
  --pattern figcraft-0.6.0-macos-universal.dmg --pattern SHA256SUMS.txt
shasum -a 256 figcraft-0.6.0-macos-universal.dmg
mkdir mounted
hdiutil attach -nobrowse -readonly -noautoopen \
  -mountpoint "$work/mounted" "$work/figcraft-0.6.0-macos-universal.dmg"
# Detach the image even if a later command fails or the shell exits.
trap 'hdiutil detach "$work/mounted"' EXIT
xattr -l "$work/mounted/FigCraft.app"
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "$work/mounted/FigCraft.app"
codesign --verify --deep --verbose=2 "$work/mounted/FigCraft.app"
ditto "$work/mounted/FigCraft.app" "$work/copied/FigCraft.app"
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "$work/copied/FigCraft.app"
xattr -dr com.apple.FinderInfo "$work/copied/FigCraft.app"
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "$work/copied/FigCraft.app"
spctl --assess --type execute -vv "$work/copied/FigCraft.app"
hdiutil detach "$work/mounted"
trap - EXIT

Run the commands individually or in a shell without set -e, so the expected failing checks do not skip the controls. No re-signing, quarantine removal, installed-app modification or GUI launch is involved.

Expected behavior

The signed app should retain strict signature validity when delivered in the finished DMG and copied out for installation. The packaging script already requires strict app verification before imaging, and the release verifier describes its purpose as checking artifacts exactly as users download them. The downloaded app should pass that same strict check without the recipient removing extended attributes.

Actual behavior

One fresh download and mount reproduced the failure once on the mounted app and once on its untouched copy. xattr -l on the mounted bundle exits 0 and lists com.apple.FinderInfo. Strict verification exits 1 on both paths. Representative output below replaces the disposable directory with /tmp/... and omits the additional affected resource paths:

$ xattr -l /tmp/.../mounted/FigCraft.app
com.apple.FinderInfo:

$ codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 /tmp/.../mounted/FigCraft.app
file with invalid attached data: Disallowed xattr com.apple.FinderInfo found on /tmp/.../mounted/FigCraft.app/Contents/Resources/FigCraft.icns
file with invalid attached data: Disallowed xattr com.apple.FinderInfo found on /tmp/.../mounted/FigCraft.app/Contents/Resources/Licenses/OFL-inter.txt
/tmp/.../mounted/FigCraft.app: resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed

The non-strict verification control on the mounted app exits 0 and reports valid on disk and satisfies its Designated Requirement. On the copy, removing only FinderInfo exits 0; the subsequent strict check exits 0 with those same success messages. The Gatekeeper assessment of that copy exits 0 and reports accepted and source=Notarized Developer ID. This isolates the observed strict-mode failure to the prohibited metadata; it does not establish a launch failure or invalid notarization.

Evidence

  • Expected source: the packaging script's strict app check and the release verifier's stated as-downloaded contract.
  • Failure source: The fresh official-asset reproduction, checksum, exit statuses and representative diagnostics recorded inline above.
  • Evidence provenance: observed
  • Local verification: reproduced
  • Reproduction completeness: complete

The DMG construction block uses hdiutil makehybrid -hfs followed by hdiutil convert, after the strict app check. Its later codesign check targets the DMG container. The release verifier's DMG block also checks the container without mounting and checking the enclosed app. These are inspection findings, not a controlled reproduction of the build process, so the exact metadata-introduction step remains unproven.

The same failure class is described in CADCraft issue #543. The open proposals CADCraft PR #637 and DeckCraft PR #175 include verification of the app inside the finished image and a copy taken from it. They are related proposals, not merged fixes or FigCraft duplicates.

Restoration check

Download a newly packaged release, mount it read-only and verify the enclosed app with codesign --verify --deep --strict. Copy it out with ditto and repeat the same check before changing any attributes. Both checks should exit 0. Keep Developer ID signing and notarization intact, and confirm Gatekeeper accepts the copied app as notarized. The current disposable-copy attribute-removal control demonstrates that this strict verification result can be restored without re-signing; it is not a substitute for validating the artifact users receive.

Triage assessment

  • Impact level: P2
  • Assessment status: supported
  • Impact basis: The official macOS artifact fails a strict signature-integrity check on both its enclosed app and a copied app, so consumers using that check reject the artifact. No GUI launch failure, data loss or notarization rejection was established; population reach beyond the tested environment is unmeasured.
  • Workaround status: available
  • Workaround basis: Removing only com.apple.FinderInfo recursively from a disposable copy restored strict verification, with no re-signing or quarantine removal, and Gatekeeper still accepted it as notarized. The recipient must perform an extra metadata-cleanup step before strict validation succeeds.

#316 [Bug Report] Intermittent graphical corruption on Fedora 44 KDE Wayland with hybrid Intel/NVIDIA graphics

classified in this triage · opened 2026-10-14 by AleixRB · updated 2026-10-17

Triage note: Hybrid Intel/NVIDIA on nouveau: severe corruption with the default Vulkan device; works when forced to Intel or lavapipe. Prefer the integrated/low-power adapter (wgpu PowerPreference) or blacklist nouveau for Vulkan, and expose a backend/adapter override.

FigCraft intermittently displays severe graphical corruption, making the application interface difficult or impossible to use. The issue occurs when running the Flatpak with the default graphics configuration.

Testing different Vulkan ICDs suggests that the issue may be related to the NVIDIA nouveau rendering path or automatic Vulkan device selection on a hybrid Intel/NVIDIA system. The application appears to work correctly when explicitly forced to use the Intel Vulkan driver or Mesa's software Vulkan renderer (lavapipe).

The exact root cause has not yet been confirmed.

System environment

  • OS: Fedora Linux 44
  • Desktop environment: KDE Plasma 6.7.5
  • Display protocol: Wayland
  • GPU 1: Intel UHD Graphics 620 (Kaby Lake-R GT2)
  • Intel kernel driver: i915
  • GPU 2: NVIDIA GeForce MX130 (GM108M)
  • NVIDIA kernel driver: nouveau
  • Application version: FigCraft 0.6.0
  • Installation method: Flatpak
  • Flatpak runtime: org.freedesktop.Platform/x86_64/26.08
  • Application ID: ai.storyteller.figcraft

Steps to reproduce

  1. Run FigCraft using its default Flatpak configuration:

    flatpak run ai.storyteller.figcraft

  2. Use the application normally until graphical corruption occurs.

  3. Restart the application with different Vulkan ICDs to compare the results.

Actual behavior

Under the default graphics configuration, the application sometimes displays severe graphical corruption, with repetitive visual patterns covering most of the application window.

The issue is intermittent.

Expected behavior

FigCraft should render its interface correctly and consistently when running under Fedora Linux with KDE Plasma Wayland and hybrid Intel/NVIDIA graphics.

Diagnostic tests

The following tests were performed by explicitly selecting Vulkan ICDs.

1. Mesa lavapipe (software rendering)

Command:

flatpak run \
  --env=VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/lvp_icd.x86_64.json \
  ai.storyteller.figcraft

Result: The graphical corruption was not observed during testing.

2. Intel UHD Graphics 620

Command:

flatpak run \
  --env=VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json \
  ai.storyteller.figcraft

Result: The application appeared to work correctly during testing.

3. NVIDIA GeForce MX130 (nouveau)

Command:

flatpak run \
  --env=VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nouveau_icd.x86_64.json \
  ai.storyteller.figcraft

Result: The graphical corruption occurred.

4. GPU power preference

The following command was also tested:

flatpak run \
  --env=WGPU_POWER_PREF=high \
  ai.storyteller.figcraft

Result: The issue persisted.

Relevant logs

The application produced the following warnings during testing:

WARN egui_winit::clipboard:
Failed to initialize arboard clipboard:
X11 server connection timed out because it was unreachable

WARN zbus::proxy:
Failed to populate properties cache via GetAll:
org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown

WARN tiny_skia::painter:
empty paths and horizontal/vertical lines cannot be filled

These warnings have not been confirmed as the cause of the graphical corruption. The clipboard and D-Bus warnings may be unrelated.

Suspected cause

The results suggest a possible compatibility issue involving Vulkan rendering on hybrid Intel/NVIDIA systems, potentially related to:

  • NVIDIA nouveau Vulkan driver compatibility.
  • Automatic Vulkan physical-device selection.
  • wgpu backend/device initialization or adapter selection.
  • Interaction between the rendering backend and the Wayland graphics stack.

The fact that both the Intel Vulkan driver and lavapipe appear to work correctly, while the nouveau test reproduces the problem, makes the NVIDIA rendering path a useful starting point for further investigation.

However, the default configuration has not yet been conclusively linked to a specific Vulkan adapter, and the exact root cause remains unknown.

Additional information

The issue persisted after updating the installed Flatpak applications and runtimes and testing WGPU_POWER_PREF=high.

The current workaround is to force the Intel Vulkan ICD:

flatpak run \
  --env=VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json \
  ai.storyteller.figcraft

This workaround appears effective during testing and does not require changing system-wide graphics drivers.

#1220 Backspace deletes a whole Thai cluster instead of the last mark

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-23 by Salah1St · updated 2026-10-23

Backspace in a text layer deletes the whole grapheme cluster before the caret (text.edit.key, via grapheme_step(…, false) in crates/engine/src/textedit.rs). For Thai, a cluster is a consonant with all its vowel and tone marks: in น้ำ ("water": น, MAI THO U+0E49, SARA AM U+0E33) one Backspace removes all three, so fixing a wrong tone mark means typing the syllable again.

Thai users (and users of Indic scripts, with their vowel signs and viramas) expect Backspace to remove the last code point, the mark typed last, as browser text fields and the operating systems' text controls do. The arrow keys moving by grapheme cluster, and Delete removing the cluster after the caret, are fine as they are.

Repro (0.10.0)

  1. Text tool, type น้ำ.
  2. Press Backspace once.
  3. Expected น้ (SARA AM removed); the layer is empty instead.

Proposal: with nothing selected, Backspace deletes only the last code point of the cluster before the caret when that code point extends a letter (Grapheme_Cluster_Break Extend or SpacingMark, e.g. Thai, Lao and Indic marks and Latin combining accents), and the whole cluster otherwise, so emoji sequences, flags and CR LF still go in one press. Delete and the arrow keys stay grapheme-based. A regression test next to grapheme_clusters in crates/text/src/behaviour_tests.rs. Size: small.

#1214 Release: re-pin craft-fonts to a commit with both the Latin manifest and Noto Sans Thai

maintainer labelshared · opened 2026-10-23 by Salah1St · updated 2026-10-23

release.yml builds every release with craft-fonts 43913056 (the pr/latin-presentation-fonts branch, storytold/craft-fonts#8), because crates/text/build.rs needs its fonts/latin-manifest.txt (Inter) under CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1. That commit predates the faces added on craft-fonts' main since, Noto Sans Thai (storytold/craft-fonts#18) among them, and main has no Latin manifest. So no release can embed a Thai face, and in the web build, which has no system fonts, Thai is always drawn as missing-glyph boxes.

storytold/craft-fonts#42 merges main into storytold/craft-fonts#8's branch, so its result has both. The comment above craft-fonts-ref in release.yml and docs/releasing.md already plan to re-pin once one commit has both, for Noto Sans Georgian; this issue adds Thai as a reason and tracks it. After the re-pin:

  • desktop packages embed Noto Sans Thai, as they embed every craft-fonts family;
  • a web build can embed it with FIGCRAFT_WEB_FONTS (#1213).

Checked against storytold/craft-fonts#42's head (ca3d91f) with CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1: figcraft-text builds for the desktop and for wasm32, and its tests pass. Until the re-pin, distributions that need Thai build with their own craft-fonts checkout.

  • FigCraft v0.9.0
  • macOS, using the trackpad

Steps to reproduce

  1. On a Mac trackpad, turn on Tap to click, with secondary click set to "Click or tap with two fingers".
  2. Open a file and tap the canvas with two fingers, without pressing down.
  3. The context menu flashes and closes.
  4. Press down with two fingers instead. The menu stays open.

Likely cause

I haven't confirmed this by running it. It comes from reading the code.

  • crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs:603 opens the menu on resp.secondary_clicked(), which fires on the button's release.
  • crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:948 closes the menu when pointer.any_pressed() is true and the pointer isn't over the menu.
  • A tap sends the press and the release almost together, so both usually land in the same egui frame. The release opens the menu. In that same frame, the press counts as a press outside a menu that has only just appeared, so the menu closes.
  • A physical click spreads the press and release over several frames, so the problem doesn't show.

Possible fix

Ignore the press that arrives in the frame the menu opens. The command palette already does this with its palette_armed flag (menus.rs, fn palette).

Workaround

Press the trackpad down with two fingers instead of tapping.

#1121 [Audit] Minor 12: Client-side maps unbounded

maintainer labelmultiple issues · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Low
Category: Minor (unbounded memory)
Location: crates/collab-net/src/inbox.rs:55-59, :63-68; crates/collab-net/src/join.rs:175, :227-233; crates/collab/src/server.rs:55-57, :449, :452

Summary: Client-side presence and peer maps grow without bound from a hostile server, and the server's deleted set never shrinks.

Detail (from code):

  • Presence map (inbox.rs:19, :55-59): BTreeMap<u32, Presence> has no size cap (unlike the events queue's MAX_EVENTS); it is only cleared by the next drain() (mem::take, lines 65-68) or a matching PeerLeft.
  • Peer list (join.rs:175, :227-233): Seen.peers grows on every unique PeerJoined and only shrinks when the same client_id sends PeerLeft or a new Welcome resets it — no cap on distinct ids.
  • Server.deleted (server.rs:55-57, :452): self.deleted.extend(applied.deleted) grows on every accepted delete; it shrinks only when a node with that id is re-created (:449). Unlike issued (capped by MAX_REMEMBERED = 65_536, server.rs:81,217-223), deleted has no cap.

Impact: A hostile server can mint unlimited fake peer/presence ids and grow client memory without bound; over a long session every deleted node id is retained forever, an unbounded server-side leak that also grows the journaled session state.

Suggested fix: Cap presence/peers maps (evict old entries), and cap or periodically compact Server.deleted.

for (_, _, s) in &spans {

// library_server.rs:161-179
pub fn refresh_server_libraries(&mut self) {
    let Ok(doc) = self.doc() else { return };
    let jobs: Vec<(String, LibraryReq)> = doc.libraries.enabled.iter()
        .filter(|l| is_server_link(&l.path))
        .map(|l| { ...; (l.path.clone(), LibraryReq::Fetch { have, usage: Some(usage(doc, &l.id)) }) })
        .collect();
    if let (false, Some(net)) = (jobs.is_empty(), self.live.link()) { net.library_background(jobs); }

  • The trigger is the Assets panel rendering (assets_panel::show → refresh_libraries, throttled by SERVER_REFRESH, immediate for unfetched links), not literally the file-open event; it happens only if the document enables marked-library links. The fetch carries the stored link including its token= query.

Impact: Opening/displaying an untrusted figure with enabled server-library links silently contacts the named servers with a stable per-file capability token — tracking/exfiltration beacon, plus slow opens.

Suggested fix: Never auto-contact library servers on open/display; fetch only on explicit user action; strip token= from automatic requests; show the hosts being contacted.

classified in this triageshared · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Triage note: Self-rated Low-Medium. Same root as critical #1056 (UNC paths leak NTLM credentials): refuse UNC/\\?\UNC roots and paths before any canonicalize/stat touches the network. Fix together with #1056.

Severity: Low-Medium
Category: Credential leak
Location:

  • crates/engine/src/file_access.rs:129-160 (resolve), :61-62 (Roots::check)
    Summary: Automation roots canonicalize UNC paths before refusing them (classic TOCTOU window).
    Status: Plausible

Verified (from code):

fn resolve(path: &Path) -> std::result::Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let abs = std::path::absolute(path).map_err(...)?;
    loop {
        match std::fs::canonicalize(at) {
            Ok(mut base) => { base.extend(rest.iter().rev()); return Ok(base); }
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => { ... rest.push(name); at = at.parent()...; }
            Err(e) => return Err(e.to_string()),
        }
    }
}
  • Resolution (following symlinks) happens before the root-boundary comparison; the I/O uses the resolved path. This is mostly defense (symlink escape is rejected); the residual gap is a TOCTOU window between resolve and the later open/read, plus Windows case/alias nuances in starts_with.

Impact: Low under the stated threat model; concurrent filesystem changes could redirect an allowed path outside the roots (and canonicalizing a UNC path contacts the SMB host before refusal).

Suggested fix: Re-verify after open (compare fstat identity / canonical path of the opened handle) or use no-follow/openat-style handles.

let free = |occ: &Vec<Vec<bool>>, c: usize, r: usize, cs: usize, rs: usize| {
    (r..r + rs).all(|ri| occ.get(ri).is_none_or(|row| (c..c + cs).all(|ci| !row.get(ci).copied().unwrap_or(false))))
};
// (None, None) => { scan from cursor: while r <= last_row { if c + cs <= cols && free(...) { ... } c += 1; ... } }

Suggested fix: Track free runs per row (interval/skip list or "next free column" pointers) so finding a free span is amortized O(cs).

    Summary: Per-area decompression caps add up to ~8GB (actually ~10GB) for one .figcraft.

Verified (from code):

// lib.rs:60

  • The caps are per-area, not a single shared budget, and several are held simultaneously. The real sum is ~10GB (document 4 + images 4 + versions 1 + branches 1), plus ~1.5GB more if a published library is present.

Impact: An untrusted .figcraft can force ~10+GB of simultaneous allocations — memory-exhaustion on modest machines.

Suggested fix: Introduce one shared global decompressed-byte budget across document/images/versions/branches/library (decrement from a common pool).

#1077 [Audit] FMT-5: Instance expansion of uncounted layers / override cloning is quadratic (Medium)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Medium
Category: DoS (CPU)
Location:

  • crates/format/src/fig/map.rs:870 (VARIABLE/VARIABLE_SET), :967-970 (per-instance visit), :2004-2012,2057-2058 (override cloning)
    Summary: Instance expansion of uncounted layers / override cloning is quadratic.
    Status: Confirmed (timing not measured)

Verified (from code):

// map.rs:870
"VARIABLE" | "VARIABLE_SET" => return None,    // after depth/count checks; count += 1 is at :881
// map.rs:967-970
for c in self.children(&sym) {
    kids.extend(self.layer_filtered(&c, Some(&sub), child_space, Some(&view), fit, depth + 1, None));
}
// map.rs:2004-2012
if let Some(inherited) = outer {
    for (path, rows) in inherited.overrides.iter() {
        let mut path = path.clone(); ... overrides.entry(path).or_default().extend(rows.iter().cloned());
    }
}
  • Variable layers are visited per child of every expanded instance but return None without consuming count, so each instance re-walks them; per nested instance the full inherited override map (paths + rows) plus props/slot_contents are deep-cloned — O(depth x overrides).

Impact: Redundant traversal of metadata layers per instance expansion; for deeply nested instance chains, repeated full override copies dominate import time.

Suggested fix: Filter VARIABLE/VARIABLE_SET out earlier so they aren't visited per instance; share override maps via Rc/Arc instead of cloning.

#1074 [Audit] SRV-2: Join/leave of an idle file causes I/O amplification on the hub thread (Medium)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Medium
Category: DoS (I/O amplification)
Location:

  • apps/figcraft-server/src/store.rs:1106-1108 (load), :1388-1394 (idle)
  • crates/collab-net/src/disk.rs:81,84 (write_atomic)
    Summary: Join and leave of an idle file reloads it and rewrites it with ~8–10 fsyncs.
    Status: Plausible

Verified (from code):

// store.rs:1106-1108
self.touch(file);
let dir = self.dir(file);
let (generation, state) = disk::decode_snapshot(&disk::read_capped(&dir.join(SNAPSHOT), self.snapshot_cap())?)?;
// store.rs:1388-1394
let dirty = self.files.get_mut(file).and_then(|e| e.log.as_mut()).is_some_and(|log| { let _ = flush_log(file, log); log.dirty });
if dirty { self.compact(file, server); }
  • touch rewrites meta.json via write_atomic (tmp sync_all + sync_dir); flush_log adds sync_data; a dirty file then compact→rewrite rewrites snapshot+log+meta (≈6 fsyncs), then idle touches again (~11 total on Unix; ~4 for a clean file).

Impact: Each join/leave of a public file costs multiple full-file rewrites and fsyncs — a cheap CPU/IO amplification vector and disk wear.

Suggested fix: Batch/defer touch; skip compaction on leave if the snapshot already contains the log's state; hold recently-used sessions open instead of reloading.

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Medium
Category: Quota bypass
Location:

    Summary: Per-address storage quotas count only the exact /64, not the documented /56 and /48.
    Status: Confirmed

Verified (from code):

// store.rs:528-529
let ip_text = ip.to_string();

  • docs/server.md:414-420 promises x2 per /56 and x4 per /48. The store never aggregates over blocks (only abuse.rs rate buckets do).

Suggested fix: Compute per-block aggregates with ip_blocks(ip) and enforce max_files_per_ip * times / max_bytes_per_ip * times per block at publish and in room_for.

#1070 [Audit] COL-8: Kicked connections aren't shut and keep their queue budget (Medium)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Medium
Category: DoS
Location:

  • crates/collab-net/src/hub.rs:1594-1601 (kick), :813-818 (refuse), :1432-1433 (remove_peer), :1545-1551 (revoke)
    Summary: Kicked or removed connections are forgotten but not shut, and keep their queue budget (up to 160MiB each).
    Status: Plausible

Verified (from code):

// hub.rs:1594-1601
fn kick(&mut self, conns: &[u64], why: &str) {
    for conn in conns {
        if let Some(c) = self.conns.get(conn) { refuse(&c.out, why); }
        self.gone(*conn);
    }
}
// hub.rs:813-818
fn refuse(out: &Line, why: &str) {
    if let Some(b) = encode(&ServerMsg::Refused { reason: why.to_string() }) {
        let _ = out.tx.try_send(Out::Bytes(b, None));
    }
    let _ = out.tx.try_send(Out::Close(CloseCode::Policy, reason(why)));
}
  • kick/remove_peer/revoke do a best-effort try_send then gone() — never shutdown(&c.sock) (unlike drop_conns at :1584-1591). If the output queue is full, try_send fails silently and the socket stays open.

Impact: Kicked/removed connections linger up to idle_timeout, retaining a max_connections slot, per-address count, thread, socket and queue memory; a stuck client is never told it was kicked.

Suggested fix: Mirror drop_conns — call shutdown(&c.sock) after gone() (or fall back to shutdown when the try_send of Close fails).

#1067 [Audit] COL-5: Id-space exhaustion blocks all future joins (Medium)

maintainer label · opened 2026-10-22 by PierrunoYT · updated 2026-10-22

Severity: Medium
Category: DoS (join)
Location:

  • crates/collab/src/server.rs:105 (next_client), :152 (restore), :276-278 (refuse), :494-499 (check_entries)
  • crates/doc/src/ids.rs:29-31 (space_of), :132-140 (highest_id_space)
    Summary: Unissued id spaces accepted; after a reload next_client = u32::MAX and nobody can join.
    Status: Confirmed

Verified (from code):

// server.rs:105
let next_client = doc.highest_id_space().saturating_add(1);
// server.rs:152
server.next_client = server.next_client.max(state.next_client);
// server.rs:276-278
if resume.is_none() && self.next_client == u32::MAX {
    return Err(refuse("no client ids left in this session"));
}
// server.rs:494-499 (check_entries): only rejects a space issued to a DIFFERENT client
  • An entry whose id space is neither the sender's nor issued to anyone passes silently; space_of maps any id with high bits >= 2^32 to u32::MAX (ids.rs:30).
  • If a document contains an id in space u32::MAX, next_client saturates to u32::MAX on new() and is kept by restore(), so every fresh join hits the line 276 refusal permanently.

Impact: Namespace/uniqueness guarantees weaken (two clients can collide on unissued-space ids), and a crafted document can permanently brick new joins after reload — a persistence-level DoS.

Suggested fix: Reject new entries whose space is neither 0 nor exactly from; treat u32::MAX as exhausted only when actually incremented past the top; give restore a Result error path when the saved id space is exhausted.

#1025 Feature request: fetch/embed Google Fonts instead of relying only on locally installed fonts

maintainer labelmultiple issues · opened 2026-10-22 by rickbenetti · updated 2026-10-22

Problem

FigCraft currently resolves font families only against what's installed locally on the system (consistent with existing reports like #934 "Custom fonts are not available" and #963 "fails to detect newly installed local fonts on Linux").

This becomes a real issue the moment a document uses a web font that the user hasn't manually installed. For example, I built a small design system file using Inter and JetBrains Mono — both popular Google Fonts, commonly used in web projects — and the only way to get them rendering correctly was to make sure they were already installed as system fonts. If I share the .figcraft file with someone who hasn't installed those fonts themselves, the document silently falls back to whatever default, with no prompt and no way to fix it from inside the app.

Figma solves this by fetching Google Fonts on demand and embedding what's used when a file is opened on a machine without those fonts installed, so the file is portable regardless of what's installed on the viewer's machine. FigCraft being used to design for the web makes this gap more noticeable than it might be for a general design tool.

Proposed solution

  • Let FigCraft query the Google Fonts API (or ship a bundled/cached subset of the catalog) and offer those families in the font picker even when not locally installed.
  • Download the font file on first use per document, cache it locally, and reference it from the .figcraft file in a way that lets any machine resolve the same family without manual installation.
  • At minimum, show a clear indicator in the font picker/inspector when a used font is NOT locally resolvable, instead of silently substituting it.

Alternatives considered

  • Manually installing every font a document references works, but breaks the moment a file is shared or opened on a different machine — which defeats a big part of the point of a portable .figcraft file.

Environment

  • figcraft-cli 0.6.0, macOS (Mach-O universal: x86_64 + arm64)

#1013 [Feature Request] [FigCraft] Add video to files

maintainer labelenhancementin progress · opened 2026-10-21 by ticket-craft[bot] · updated 2026-10-21

Description

Figma doesn't have a specific layer type for video, instead, videos are a type of fill. Since videos are fills, you can add them to any vector or shape.

There are a number of ways you can add video to design files:

A. Drag and drop video file from your computer onto the canvas.
B. Use the video importer from the fill color picker.
C. Use the Place image/video tool to add videos in bulk.
D. Copy a video from another layer in the current file, or from another file.
E. Paste any video from your clipboard into the canvas.

Note: You can also add animated GIFs to prototypes. GIFs only playback when viewing designs and prototypes in presentation view.

If you add a video straight to the canvas, Figma creates an object on the canvas with the dimensions of the original file. If you add a video as a fill to an existing object, Figma uses the name and dimensions of the original object.

View and update video fills in the Fill section of the right sidebar. From the Fill section, you can play and preview your video fill, jump to a specific timestamp, or scrub through the video.

You can also identify layers with video fills in the Layers panel in the left sidebar. Objects with video fills are represented on the layers panel with a play icon.

Edit video

Once you’ve added a video to your file, you can edit the video in the following ways:

Scale, rotate and adjust the dimensions of any layers with video
Crop and re-position video applied to layers
Adjust the video options including the Fill mode, rotation and blend modes
Apply masks to only show a part of the video
Prototype with video

Once you add video to a frame, switch over to the Prototype of the right sidebar. From here, you can create interactions between frames with video.

For more ideas about supporting Figma video layers:
https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/8878274530455-Use-videos-in-prototypes

I think I found the cause. The Individual corners fields were laid out in storage order (top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left), so the bottom row showed bottom right on the left and bottom left on the right. All four fields also used the same top-left icon, so nothing showed which was which. In your screenshot "0 | 30" in the bottom row really meant bottom right 0, bottom left 30.

I've opened a PR that puts each field at its corner (top left, top right / bottom left, bottom right) with its own corner icon.

About the pen tool comment: vectors drawn with the pen take one radius for all their corners, so they don't show these four fields. If something else goes wrong there (for example the radius has no effect on a pen shape), could you open a separate issue with the steps?
